VI. CONCLUSION
In this paper, we demonstrate that the holdout method
can significantly decrease the sample complexity in finding
probabilistically tight reachable sets; this method is highly
efficient when collecting scenarios is computationally cheap.
Furthermore, we complement our work with a discussion on
the necessity of probabilistic reachability bounds within the
context of data-driven analysis.
